🤝 MSCS — Moral, Social & Cultural Studies (20 marks)

ChapterPagesYou must be able to…
1. What is meant by duties and responsibilities?Vol 1, p. 8–16Analyse why moral and ethical principles matter for social harmony • explain and evaluate the Ministry of Education's strategic goals • compare students' duties in Japan, the UAE and India
2. Duties and responsibilities of parents towards their childrenVol 1, p. 17–26Explain the key provisions of Wadeema's Law • apply it to real-life situations • evaluate why parental responsibilities matter
3. Culture through art in ChinaVol 1, p. 176–183Describe life in 18th-century China from Qing paintings • discuss the Qianlong Emperor's Southern Inspection Tour
4. Human needsVol 2, p. 58–90Analyse basic human needs and why they matter • evaluate arguments for and against conflict as a response to unmet needs, with evidence
5. GlobalisationVol 2, p. 8–46Explain globalisation and how it affects the UAE • a sustainable global economy and its challenges • the impact of communication technology

✍️ Command words in MSCS

WordWhat to do
ExplainSay what it is and why/how, with an example.
AnalyseBreak it into parts; show causes, effects and links.
EvaluateGive strengths and weaknesses, then a judgement ("Overall, I think… because…").
CompareSimilarities and differences — a table works well.
ApplyUse the rule/law on the situation given: name the rule → link to the facts → conclusion.
Reasoned judgement formula: Claim → Evidence for → Evidence against → Judgement with your main reason.

1. Key words

WordMeaningExample
DutySomething you must do because of your role, the law or moralityA student's duty to attend school
ResponsibilitySomething you are trusted with and accountable for; you answer for the resultsBeing responsible for your class pet or a group project
ObligationSomething you are bound to do by a law, rule, promise or agreementKeeping a promise; paying for what you buy
RightSomething you are entitled toThe right to education
Morals / ethicsPrinciples about what is right and wrong that guide behaviourHonesty, fairness, respect

Rights and duties go together: my right to learn means I have a duty not to disturb others' learning.

We have duties at different levels: to ourselves (health, learning), our family, our school, our community and country, and to the environment.

2. Moral and ethical principles and social harmony

PrincipleWhat it looks likeImpact on the community
Honesty & integrityTelling the truth, not cheatingBuilds trust between people
RespectTreating everyone with dignity, listeningFewer conflicts; people feel valued
ToleranceAccepting people of other cultures, religions and opinionsPeaceful living in diverse societies
Justice / fairnessSame rules for everyonePeople accept decisions; less anger
Kindness & compassionHelping those in need, volunteeringStronger community bonds
Responsibility & cooperationDoing your part, working togetherThings get done; shared success
UAE example: with over 200 nationalities living together, the UAE promotes tolerance — it created a Ministry of Tolerance (2016), named 2019 the Year of Tolerance, and opened the Abrahamic Family House in Abu Dhabi (2023), with a mosque, a church and a synagogue side by side.
Q: Analyse the impact on a community if people stopped following moral principles.

Trust would break down (lying, cheating), conflicts and crime would rise, people would feel unsafe and stop cooperating, and weaker members would be treated unfairly. Social harmony depends on shared values such as honesty, respect and tolerance.

3. The Ministry of Education's strategic goals

The UAE Ministry of Education (MoE) sets strategic goals to build a first-rate education system that prepares students for the future and supports the national vision ("We the UAE 2031"). The main goals include:

GoalHow it improves education
Inclusive, high-quality education for all, including early childhoodEvery child — including students of determination — gets a good start and equal chances
World-class student achievementModern curriculum, international tests (PISA, TIMSS), skills like critical thinking and innovation
A safe, healthy and stimulating school environmentAnti-bullying and behaviour policies, health and wellbeing programmes
Strengthening values, national identity and responsibilityMSCS, Arabic and Islamic studies, volunteering — good citizens, not just good grades
Qualified, motivated teachers and school leadersTeacher licensing and training
Innovation, technology and researchSmart learning, AI and coding in schools, links to higher education
Efficient, transparent servicesEasy e-services for parents and students

ℹ️ Check the exact wording of the goals in your textbook (p. 8–16) — the ideas are the same.

Evaluate the goals

Strengths 👍Challenges 👎
Prepare students for a knowledge economy; focus on values as well as grades; inclusion of all learners; use of technologyNeed lots of money and trained teachers; pressure from tests; technology can widen gaps if not everyone has access; goals need time to show results

4. Students' duties: Japan vs the UAE vs India

Area🇯🇵 Japan🇦🇪 UAE🇮🇳 India
CleaningStudents clean their own classrooms, corridors and toilets every day (o-soji)Keep classrooms tidy; cleaning mostly done by staffKeep the classroom neat; cleanliness drives (Swachh Bharat); cleaning mostly done by staff
LunchStudents serve lunch to classmates in turns and clear upHealthy eating rules; canteen or packed lunchPacked lunch or mid-day meal; sharing food
RespectBow and greet teachers; group harmony (wa) is very importantRespect teachers and classmates; Islamic and Emirati values; respect for all culturesStrong respect for teachers (guru–shishya tradition); Teachers' Day on 5 September
Rules & disciplinePunctuality, uniforms, walking to school in groupsFollow the MoE Student Behaviour Policy (points for misbehaviour), attendance rules, uniformUniforms, discipline, homework; respect national symbols (Fundamental Duties)
Assembly / identityMorning meetings, school eventsMorning assembly with the national anthem, National Day celebrationsMorning assembly with prayer and the national anthem
CommunityClub activities, caring for the schoolVolunteering, caring for heritage and environmentSocial service, eco clubs

Similarities: all expect respect for teachers, punctuality, uniforms, hard work and good behaviour. Key differences: Japanese students take on practical responsibilities (cleaning, serving lunch), which teaches responsibility and teamwork; the UAE has a formal behaviour points system and stresses national identity and tolerance; India stresses respect for teachers and national symbols, with discipline and exams.

Q: Which practice from another country would you bring to your school, and why?

Example: Japan's daily cleaning — students learn responsibility, respect for their school and teamwork, and the school stays cleaner. A good answer names the practice, explains the benefit, and notes a challenge (e.g. time taken from lessons).

1. Parents' duties and responsibilities

TypeExamples
PhysicalFood, clothing, shelter, health care, vaccinations, safety
EmotionalLove, care, listening, encouragement, a stable home
EducationEnrol the child in school, support homework, work with teachers
Moral & socialTeach values (honesty, respect), religion and culture, good manners, being a role model
LegalRegister the birth, give the child a name and identity, never neglect or abuse the child
DigitalSupervise internet and screen use, protect from harmful content

2. Wadeema's Law — the UAE Child Rights Law

Federal Law No. 3 of 2016 on Child Rights, known as Wadeema's Law. It is named after Wadeema, an eight-year-old girl who died in 2012 after severe abuse and neglect at home. Her case led the UAE to create a strong law to protect every child. It covers everyone under 18.

Key provisions

ProvisionWhat it means
Right to life, safety and developmentThe state, parents and society must protect the child's life and healthy growth.
IdentityRight to a name, a registered birth and a nationality.
Family careRight to grow up in a caring family environment; parents must provide food, shelter, care and supervision.
HealthRight to health care and vaccinations; protection from harmful things (e.g. selling tobacco to children is banned).
EducationRight to education; parents must enrol their children in school.
Protection from harmProtection from all forms of violence, abuse, neglect and exploitation, including harmful online content and dangerous work (children under 15 may not be employed).
Expression and privacyRight to express opinions (according to age) and to privacy.
Duty to reportAnyone who knows a child is in danger must report it — especially teachers, doctors and social workers.
Child protection specialistsTrained officers can investigate reports and act quickly — including moving a child to safety.
PenaltiesFines and prison for people who break the law, such as neglecting or abusing a child.
Getting help in the UAE: children and adults can report concerns to a trusted adult at school, the police (999), or child protection lines such as the Ministry of Interior Child Protection Centre (116111).

How the law safeguards children

  • Makes it clear that child protection is everyone's job, not just the family's.
  • Problems are reported early, before they become dangerous.
  • Specialists can act quickly to remove a child from danger.
  • Penalties discourage abuse and neglect.
  • It follows the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child.

3. Apply it: real-life situations

A. Parents often leave their 7-year-old alone at home for whole evenings. Are they fulfilling their duties?

No. Leaving a young child without supervision exposes them to danger — this is neglect. Wadeema's Law requires parents to care for and supervise their children and protect their safety.

B. A shop sells cigarettes to a 15-year-old.

This breaks Wadeema's Law, which protects children's health and bans selling tobacco to anyone under 18. The shop can be fined.

C. A teacher notices a student often has bruises and is afraid to go home. What should she do?

Report it immediately to the school's child protection lead or a child protection specialist. Under Wadeema's Law, teachers have a duty to report suspected abuse.

D. A father helps his daughter with homework every evening, takes her for vaccinations and talks with her about online safety.

Yes, he is fulfilling his duties: education, health and protection from online harm, plus emotional support.

E. Parents keep their 12-year-old at home to work in the family shop instead of sending him to school.

Not fulfilling their duties: the child's right to education is denied, and children must not be made to work instead of studying.

4. Evaluate: why do parental responsibilities matter?

AreaEffect of responsible parenting
DevelopmentGood nutrition, sleep, play and learning help the brain and body grow; children do better at school.
SafetySupervision protects children from accidents, abuse and online dangers.
Well-beingLove and attention build confidence, happiness and good mental health.
SocietyChildren raised with good values become responsible citizens → a stronger community.

Judgement: parents are a child's first teachers and first protectors. Schools and laws help, but they cannot replace a caring family. Laws like Wadeema's Law are a safety net for when families fail.

1. China in the 18th century — the Qing dynasty

  • The Qing dynasty (1644–1912) was China's last imperial dynasty. Its rulers were Manchus from the north-east.
  • The 18th century is called the "High Qing": a long period of peace, a growing economy and a booming population (about 300 million by 1800).
  • China produced and exported silk, tea and porcelain; foreign trade was limited to the port of Guangzhou (Canton) from 1757.
  • Three great emperors: Kangxi (1661–1722), Yongzheng (1722–1735) and Qianlong (1735–1796).

2. The Qianlong Emperor

  • Ruled for about 60 years (1735–1796), then stepped down so as not to rule longer than his grandfather Kangxi.
  • Expanded the empire to its largest size.
  • A huge patron of the arts: collected thousands of paintings and objects, wrote tens of thousands of poems, and stamped his seals on artworks. Court painters included the Chinese artist Xu Yang and the Italian Jesuit Giuseppe Castiglione (Lang Shining).

3. The Southern Inspection Tours (南巡 Nanxun)

The Qianlong Emperor made six Southern Inspection Tours (1751, 1757, 1762, 1765, 1780, 1784) to the rich Jiangnan region south of the Yangtze River — cities like Suzhou, Hangzhou, Nanjing and Yangzhou — copying his grandfather Kangxi, who also made six tours.

PurposeExplanation
Inspect water worksCheck flood defences on the Yellow River, the Grand Canal and sea walls — floods could ruin farms and stop grain transport.
Show powerHuge processions showed the strength and splendour of the Manchu emperor to the southern Chinese.
Win loyaltyMet scholars and officials, held exams, reduced taxes and gave gifts to win the support of the wealthy south.
Check officials and troopsSaw for himself how local government and the army were working.
Family dutyHe took his mother on several tours — showing filial piety (respect for parents), a key Confucian value.

Criticism: the tours were extremely expensive; local people and officials had to pay for roads, palaces and entertainment.

4. Reading the paintings

The court painter Xu Yang painted "The Qianlong Emperor's Southern Inspection Tour" (completed 1770), a set of 12 long handscrolls recording the first tour of 1751. Some are now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art (New York). Xu Yang also painted "Prosperous Suzhou" (1759). Handscrolls are unrolled from right to left, like a journey.

What we seeWhat it tells us about life
Busy markets, shops with signboards, people bargainingA strong commercial economy; many trades and crafts
Boats crowding the Grand CanalRivers and canals were the main transport for grain, goods and people
Farmers in rice fields, water buffaloMost people were farmers; the land was fertile and well irrigated
Officials kneeling as the emperor passesA strict hierarchy: the emperor was supreme and treated with deep respect
Scholars, temples, gardens, theatresRich culture, Confucian learning and leisure in southern cities
Dikes and river worksThe importance of water control to the state
Paintings as historical sources: 👍 they show clothing, buildings, work and daily life in great detail. 👎 They were made for the emperor to glorify him, so they show an ideal, peaceful and prosperous picture and may hide poverty and problems. Use them alongside written records.

✅ Quick check

1. Name two reasons for the Qianlong Emperor's Southern Inspection Tours.

To inspect flood defences on the Yellow River and Grand Canal, and to show imperial power and win the loyalty of the rich south (also: check officials, honour his mother).

2. Who painted the Southern Inspection Tour scrolls and how many scrolls are there?

Xu Yang; a set of 12 handscrolls (completed 1770).

3. What do the paintings show about China's economy in the 18th century?

Busy markets, shops, crafts and canal trade show a prosperous commercial economy, supported by farming and water transport.

4. Why should historians be careful with these paintings?

They were commissioned by the emperor to glorify him, so they may exaggerate prosperity and order and leave out hardship.

1. Needs vs wants

Needs are things we must have to survive and live well (food, water, shelter, safety). Wants are things we would like but can live without (a new phone, games).

Maslow's hierarchy of needs (Abraham Maslow, 1943)

LevelNeedExamples
5 (top)Self-actualisationReaching your full potential, creativity, purpose
4EsteemRespect, confidence, achievement, recognition
3Love and belongingFamily, friends, community
2SafetySecurity, health, a job, law and order
1 (base)PhysiologicalFood, water, air, shelter, sleep, clothing

The lower needs usually have to be met before people can focus on the higher ones.

2. Why meeting needs matters

For the individualFor society
Good health and growth • ability to learn and work • mental well-being and happiness • a chance to reach their potentialProductive workers and a strong economy • stability, less crime and conflict • social harmony • people can contribute to the community
UAE example: the state supports citizens' needs through free public health care and education for nationals, housing programmes (e.g. the Sheikh Zayed Housing Programme), and is one of the world's leading donors of humanitarian aid, helping meet basic needs in other countries.

3. Is conflict a justified response to unmet needs?

When needs like food, water, land or safety are not met, tension can grow. Conflict can mean anything from disagreement and peaceful protest to violence and war.

Arguments FOR conflict 👍Arguments AGAINST conflict 👎
• When people are starving or oppressed and peaceful requests are ignored, they may feel they have no other choice.
• Peaceful protest has won rights in history (e.g. the civil rights movement in the USA).
• Defending yourself or your family's survival can be seen as natural.		 • Violent conflict destroys homes, farms, schools and hospitals, so even more needs go unmet.
• It causes deaths, injuries and refugees.
• It can last for years and create hatred between groups.
• Peaceful solutions — dialogue, negotiation, mediation, aid and cooperation — have worked many times.

Evidence you can use

  • Food price crisis (2007–2008): sharp rises in food prices led to protests and riots in many countries — unmet needs can cause unrest.
  • Lake Chad: as the lake shrank, competition for water and land added to conflict and hunger in the region.
  • Cooperation works: the Indus Waters Treaty (1960) helped India and Pakistan share river water for decades without war over it (though India suspended it in 2025 during tensions). International aid and the UN's World Food Programme feed millions instead of leaving them to fight.
Model judgement: "Although conflict can draw attention to unmet needs, I believe violent conflict is not justified, because it destroys the very resources people need and causes more suffering. Peaceful protest, negotiation and cooperation, as with the Indus Waters Treaty, are more effective ways to meet needs."

✅ Quick check

1. What is the difference between a need and a want? Give an example of each.

A need is essential for survival and well-being (water); a want is nice to have but not essential (a games console).

2. Name the five levels of Maslow's hierarchy from the bottom.

Physiological → safety → love and belonging → esteem → self-actualisation.

3. Explain why meeting basic needs is important for society.

People who are healthy, safe and educated can work and contribute; this builds a strong economy and reduces crime and conflict, creating social harmony.

4. Give one argument for and one against conflict as a response to unmet needs.

For: when peaceful requests are ignored, protest can force change. Against: violent conflict destroys resources and creates more unmet needs and refugees.

1. What is globalisation?

Globalisation is the process by which countries and people around the world become more connected and dependent on each other through trade, investment, technology, travel, migration and culture.

TypeExample
EconomicTrade, multinational companies (e.g. a phone designed in the USA, made in Asia, sold in Dubai)
CulturalFilms, music, food and fashion spread worldwide
PoliticalInternational organisations: UN, WTO, cooperation on climate
TechnologicalThe internet, social media, instant communication

Drivers: cheaper and faster transport (container ships, planes) • the internet and mobile phones • trade agreements • multinational companies • people migrating for work.

2. How globalisation affects the UAE

Benefits 👍Issues 👎
• A global trade and transport hub: Jebel Ali Port is one of the world's largest ports; Dubai International Airport is among the busiest for international travellers; Emirates and Etihad connect the world.
• Foreign investment and free zones create jobs.
• Diversifying the economy away from oil (tourism, finance, logistics).
• A multicultural society with people from over 200 nationalities.
• Hosting global events such as Expo 2020 Dubai and COP28 (2023).		 • Risk to cultural identity and the use of the Arabic language.
• Dependence on the world economy — the 2008 global financial crisis hit Dubai hard.
• Strong competition for local businesses.
• Environmental pressure (more flights, shipping, consumption).
• Diseases spread faster (COVID-19).

The UAE's response: protecting national identity and heritage (Arabic language initiatives, heritage festivals, MSCS in schools) while staying open to the world.

3. A sustainable global economy

A sustainable economy grows and creates jobs without destroying the environment or harming future generations, and shares benefits fairly.

  • Renewable energy instead of fossil fuels
  • Circular economy: reduce, reuse, recycle — waste becomes a resource
  • Fair trade and decent work
  • Protecting forests, oceans and biodiversity
UAE examples: Masdar City (Abu Dhabi), the Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Solar Park (Dubai), the Barakah nuclear power plant, the Green Economy initiative (2012), the Net Zero by 2050 strategic initiative, and hosting COP28 in Dubai, which ended with the "UAE Consensus".

Challenges

  • The world still depends heavily on oil, gas and coal.
  • Green technology can be expensive for poorer countries.
  • Inequality between rich and poor countries.
  • Overconsumption and waste.
  • Climate change, and trade disputes between countries.

4. Impact of communication technology

Positive 👍Negative 👎
IndividualInstant contact with family abroad • online learning • access to information • new skills and jobsCyberbullying • addiction and too much screen time • privacy risks and scams • less face-to-face time
CommunityE-government (e.g. UAE Pass, smart services) • distance learning during COVID-19 • e-commerce helps businesses • fast emergency alertsFake news and rumours spread quickly • cybercrime • digital divide (not everyone has access) • foreign content may weaken local values
Responsible digital citizenship: check sources before sharing, protect passwords and personal data, be kind online, balance screen time. In the UAE, spreading rumours and cybercrime are punished by law.

Evaluate: overall communication technology brings huge benefits to learning, business and staying connected, but only if people use it responsibly and governments protect users.

✅ Quick check

1. Define globalisation.

The process by which countries and people become more connected and interdependent through trade, technology, travel and culture.

2. Give two ways globalisation has benefited the UAE.

It became a global trade and transport hub (Jebel Ali, Dubai Airport), attracting investment and jobs; it helped diversify the economy away from oil (also tourism, a multicultural society).

3. Give one issue globalisation raises for the UAE.

Risk to cultural identity and the Arabic language (or dependence on the global economy, e.g. the 2008 crisis).

4. What is a sustainable global economy? Name one challenge.

An economy that grows without harming the environment or future generations; challenge: dependence on fossil fuels / high cost of green technology.

5. Evaluate the impact of social media on a community.

Positive: fast sharing of information, alerts, connecting people. Negative: fake news and cyberbullying. Judgement: beneficial if used responsibly with verified sources.

🎨 Enrichment activity

Choose a country, explore its traditional clothing, then design and colour your own outfit inspired by that culture → see the 🎨 Project tab.

⚠️ Top 6 mistakes that lose marks

  1. Colour/adjective before the noun. Arabic: noun first → قميص أحمر.
  2. Masculine colour with a feminine noun: تنورة أحمر ❌ → تنورة حمراء ✅.
  3. Forgetting that plurals of things take a feminine singular adjective: ملابس جميلة ✅.
  4. Using لا with a past verb: لا لبستُ ❌ → لم ألبسْ or ما لبستُ ✅.
  5. Adding ال to the noun but not to the adjective: القميص أبيض means "the shirt is white"; "the white shirt" = القميص الأبيض.
  6. No reasons in writing. Always add لأنّ (because).

Making أَفْعَل for تعجب

AdjectiveتعجبAdjectiveتعجب
جَميلما أَجْمَلَ …!طَويلما أَطْوَلَ …!
كَبيرما أَكْبَرَ …!واسِعما أَوْسَعَ …!

ما أَجْمَلَ دُبَيّ! is NOT a question, even though it starts with ما: it ends with ! and has أَفْعَل. That makes it أُسْلوب تَعَجُّب.

First decide what kind of word most of them are: clothes? places? verbs (يـ / تـ at the start)? adjectives? question words? connectors (و، لكن، بينما)? The odd one is the one from a different group.

راشِدٌ يُسافِرُ إلى الهِنْدِ مَعَ صَديقِهِ في عُطْلةِ الصَّيْفِ.

خالِدٌ يَذْهَبُ مَعَ أُسْرَتِهِ إلى دُكّانِ المَلابِسِ لِيَشْتَرِيَ مَلابِسَ المَدْرَسةِ.
← سارةُ تَذْهَبُ مَعَ أُسْرَتِها إلى دُكّانِ المَلابِسِ لِتَشْتَرِيَ مَلابِسَ المَدْرَسةِ.

خالِدٌ يَلْعَبُ مَعَ صَديقِهِ في المَلْعَبِ يَوْمَ الجُمُعةِ.
← سارةُ تَلْعَبُ مَعَ صَديقَتِها في المَلْعَبِ يَوْمَ الجُمُعةِ.
Don't change words that are not about the person: مَلابِسَ المَدْرَسةِ stays the same.

6. اجعل الجملة للنفي — make it negative

Present verb → put لا before the verb. (Past: لَمْ + present verb, or ما + past verb. See the Grammar tab.)

يَذْهَبُ راشِدٌ إلى مول الإماراتِ يَوْمَ الجُمُعةِ.
← لا يَذْهَبُ راشِدٌ إلى مول الإماراتِ يَوْمَ الجُمُعةِ.

الأُمُّ تُفَضِّلُ التَّسَوُّقَ مِنْ قِسْمِ مَلابِسِ الأَطْفالِ.
← الأُمُّ لا تُفَضِّلُ التَّسَوُّقَ مِنْ قِسْمِ مَلابِسِ الأَطْفالِ.

ذَهَبَ راشِدٌ إلى المول. ← لَمْ يَذْهَبْ راشِدٌ إلى المول. / ما ذَهَبَ راشِدٌ إلى المول.

7. صحّح الخطأ — correct the mistake

The mistakes are almost always about adjectives:

  1. The adjective comes after the noun: الفُسْتان النَّظيف, not نَظيفة الفُسْتان.
  2. It matches the noun: masculine/feminine, and الـ if the noun has الـ.
  3. Plural of things (not people) takes a feminine singular adjective: مَلابِسُ جَميلةٌ.
  4. The verb matches the person: أُمّي تَلْبَسُ (not يَلْبَسُ).
  5. Section names: قِسْمُ مَلابِسِ الرِّجالِ / النِّساءِ (قسم first).
WrongCorrect
أَنا أَلْبَسُ نَظيفة الفُسْتان.أَنا أَلْبَسُ الفُسْتانَ النَّظيفَ.
أَبي يَشْتَري مَلابِس جَميل مِنْ مَلابِس قِسْم الرِّجال.أَبي يَشْتَري مَلابِسَ جَميلةً مِنْ قِسْمِ مَلابِسِ الرِّجالِ.
أُخْتي تَشْتَري طَويل عَباءة وتَنّورة ضَيِّق.أُخْتي تَشْتَري عَباءةً طَويلةً وتَنّورةً ضَيِّقةً.
صَديقَتي تَلْبَسُ قَميصًا زَرْقاء وأَزْرَق مِعْطَف في المَدْرَسة.صَديقَتي تَلْبَسُ قَميصًا أَزْرَقَ ومِعْطَفًا أَزْرَقَ في المَدْرَسةِ.
أُمّي يَلْبَس طَويل عَباءة مِنْ نِساء مَلابِس القِسْم.أُمّي تَلْبَسُ عَباءةً طَويلةً مِنْ قِسْمِ مَلابِسِ النِّساءِ.

Choose the right word

يَذْهَبُ الرَّجُلُ إلى دُكّانِ المَلابِسِ لِيَشْتَرِيَ مَلابِسَ الصَّيْفِ. (لِيَشْتَرِيَ – يَبيعُ – يَلْبَسُ)
ما أَجْمَلَ التَّسَوُّقَ مَعَ العائِلةِ! (جَميلة – مُمْتِعة – ما أَجْمَلَ)

8. القراءة والفهم — how to answer

  • Answer in a full sentence that reuses the question words: أَيْنَ تَذْهَبُ الأُسْرةُ؟ ← تَذْهَبُ الأُسْرةُ إلى …
  • لِماذا → find لِأَنَّ in the text and copy the reason.
  • نَعَم / لا / لا أَعْرِف: choose لا أَعْرِف only when the text does not say.
  • صَحّ / خَطَأ: if it's wrong, say what the text really says.

The passages below are re-written versions of the ones on the sheets, with the same facts, for practice.

📖 Passage A — راشد وأسرته في دكان الملابس

يَسْكُنُ راشِدٌ في مَدينةِ دُبَيّ لِأَنَّها مَدينةٌ جَميلةٌ وفيها مَتاجِرُ كَثيرةٌ. يَوْمَ الجُمُعةِ تَذْهَبُ أُسْرَتُهُ بِالسَّيّارةِ إلى دُكّانِ المَلابِسِ. يَشْتَري الأَبُ قُفّازًا جَميلًا، ويُفَضِّلُ أَخوهُ أَنْ يَشْتَرِيَ بَدْلةً أَنيقةً، أَمّا راشِدٌ فَيُفَضِّلُ رابِطةَ عُنُقٍ. وتُفَضِّلُ الأُمُّ أَنْ تَشْتَرِيَ حِجابًا، بَيْنَما تُفَضِّلُ الأُخْتُ فُسْتانًا قَصيرًا.
وفي إِجازةِ الصَّيْفِ الماضي ذَهَبَتِ الأُسْرةُ إلى مول الإماراتِ، وشاهَدوا مَلابِسَ كَثيرةً لِلرِّجالِ والنِّساءِ. اشْتَرى الأَبُ مَلابِسَ خَفيفةً لِأَنَّ الجَوَّ كانَ حارًّا جِدًّا، والأُمُّ تُفَضِّلُ المَلابِسَ الصَّيْفيّةَ المَصْنوعةَ مِنَ القُطْنِ. اسْتَمْتَعوا كَثيرًا لِأَنَّ أَقْسامَ المَلابِسِ كَثيرةٌ ورائِعةٌ، لكِنْ لَمْ تُعْجِبْ راشِدًا الأَسْعارُ المُرْتَفِعةُ، فَالمَلابِسُ غالِيةٌ جِدًّا ولا توجَدُ تَخْفيضاتٌ.
Show English translation

Rashid lives in Dubai because it is a beautiful city with many shops. On Friday his family goes by car to the clothes shop. Father buys a nice glove, his brother prefers an elegant suit, and Rashid prefers a tie. Mother prefers a headscarf, while his sister prefers a short dress. Last summer holiday the family went to Mall of the Emirates and saw lots of men's and women's clothes. Father bought light clothes because it was very hot; mother prefers cotton summer clothes. They enjoyed it because the clothes sections are many and great, but Rashid didn't like the high prices: clothes are very expensive and there are no discounts.

Questions (tap for the answer)

أَيْنَ تَذْهَبُ الأُسْرةُ يَوْمَ الجُمُعةِ؟
تَذْهَبُ الأُسْرةُ إلى دُكّانِ المَلابِسِ.
ماذا تُفَضِّلُ الأُمُّ أَنْ تَشْتَرِيَ؟
تُفَضِّلُ الأُمُّ أَنْ تَشْتَرِيَ حِجابًا.
مَتى تَذْهَبُ الأُسْرةُ إلى دُكّانِ المَلابِسِ؟ وكَيْفَ؟
تَذْهَبُ يَوْمَ الجُمُعةِ بِالسَّيّارةِ.
لِماذا اشْتَرى الأَبُ مَلابِسَ خَفيفةً؟
لِأَنَّ الجَوَّ كانَ حارًّا جِدًّا.
الأَسْعارُ في المول كانَتْ رَخيصةً. (نَعَم – لا – لا أَعْرِف)
لا: الأَسْعارُ كانَتْ مُرْتَفِعةً ولا توجَدُ تَخْفيضاتٌ.
تُفَضِّلُ الأُمُّ المَلابِسَ المَصْنوعةَ مِنْ …… (القُطْن – الحَرير – الصّوف)
القُطْن
ذَهَبَتِ الأُسْرةُ إلى …… في فَصْلِ ……
مول الإماراتِ — في فَصْلِ الصَّيْفِ
ما الَّذي لَمْ يُعْجِبْ راشِدًا في المول؟
لَمْ تُعْجِبْهُ الأَسْعارُ المُرْتَفِعةُ وقِلّةُ التَّخْفيضاتِ.
ما رَأْيُكَ في الأَسْعارِ هُناكَ؟
في رَأْيي الأَسْعارُ مُرْتَفِعةٌ جِدًّا لِأَنَّهُ لا توجَدُ تَخْفيضاتٌ.

📖 Passage B — مريم تشتري ملابس المدرسة

في بِدايةِ العامِ الدِّراسيِّ قَرَّرَتْ مَرْيَمُ أَنْ تَذْهَبَ مَعَ والِدَتِها إلى السّوقِ لِتَشْتَرِيَ مَلابِسَ جَديدةً لِلْمَدْرَسةِ. كانَ السّوقُ كَبيرًا ومَليئًا بِالمَحَلّاتِ الواسِعةِ المُضيئةِ. دَخَلَتْ مَرْيَمُ مَحَلًّا يَبيعُ المَلابِسَ المَدْرَسيّةَ، فَرَأَتْ قُمْصانًا بَيْضاءَ وتَنانيرَ زَرْقاءَ. اخْتارَتْ قَميصًا مُريحًا وتَنّورةً بِمَقاسِها، وحِذاءً أَسْوَدَ مُناسِبًا لِلْمَدْرَسةِ. كانَتْ سَعيدةً لِأَنَّ الأَسْعارَ مُناسِبةٌ، ولِأَنَّها سَتَبْدَأُ عامَها الدِّراسيَّ بِمَلابِسَ أَنيقةٍ ونَظيفةٍ.
Show English translation

At the start of the school year Maryam decided to go with her mother to the market to buy new school clothes. The market was big and full of wide, bright shops. She went into a shop selling school uniforms and saw white shirts and blue skirts. She chose a comfortable shirt and a skirt in her size, and black shoes suitable for school. She was happy because the prices were reasonable and because she would start her school year in neat, clean clothes.

Questions (tap for the answer)

ماذا اشْتَرَتْ مَرْيَمُ؟
اشْتَرَتْ قَميصًا مُريحًا وتَنّورةً وحِذاءً أَسْوَدَ.
لِماذا كانَتْ مَرْيَمُ سَعيدةً بَعْدَ التَّسَوُّقِ؟
لِأَنَّ الأَسْعارَ مُناسِبةٌ، ولِأَنَّها سَتَبْدَأُ عامَها الدِّراسيَّ بِمَلابِسَ أَنيقةٍ ونَظيفةٍ.
صِفِ السّوقَ.
كانَ السّوقُ كَبيرًا ومَليئًا بِالمَحَلّاتِ الواسِعةِ المُضيئةِ.
مَرْيَمُ اشْتَرَتْ حَقيبةً جَديدةً. (صَحّ / خَطَأ)
خَطَأ ✗: اشْتَرَتْ قَميصًا وتَنّورةً وحِذاءً.
السّوقُ كانَ كَبيرًا. (صَحّ / خَطَأ)
صَحّ ✓

📖 Passage C — خالد ويوسف في المركز التجاري

في عُطْلةِ نِهايةِ الأُسْبوعِ ذَهَبَ خالِدٌ مَعَ صَديقِهِ يوسُفَ إلى مَرْكَزٍ تِجاريٍّ جَديدٍ في المَدينةِ. كانَ المَكانُ واسِعًا، وفيهِ طَوابِقُ كَثيرةٌ ومَحَلّاتٌ مُتَنَوِّعةٌ. دَخَلَ خالِدٌ مَتْجَرَ المَلابِسِ الرِّياضيّةِ، فَاشْتَرى قَميصًا رِياضيًّا وحِذاءً مُريحًا لِلَعِبِ كُرةِ القَدَمِ. أَمّا يوسُفُ فَفَضَّلَ شِراءَ جاكيتٍ شِتْويٍّ لِأَنَّهُ يَسْتَعِدُّ لِفَصْلِ الشِّتاءِ. بَعْدَ التَّسَوُّقِ جَلَسَ الصَّديقانِ في مَطْعَمٍ داخِلَ المَرْكَزِ التِّجاريِّ، وتَحَدَّثا عَنْ هِواياتِهِما المُفَضَّلةِ، واتَّفَقا عَلى اللَّعِبِ مَعًا في المَلْعَبِ القَريبِ يَوْمَ الجُمُعةِ القادِمِ.
Show English translation

At the weekend Khalid went with his friend Youssef to a new mall in the city. The place was wide, with many floors and different shops. Khalid went into the sports clothes shop and bought a sports shirt and comfortable football shoes. Youssef preferred to buy a winter jacket because he is getting ready for winter. After shopping the two friends sat in a restaurant inside the mall, talked about their favourite hobbies, and agreed to play together at the nearby playground next Friday.

Questions (tap for the answer)

ماذا اشْتَرى يوسُفُ؟
اشْتَرى يوسُفُ جاكيتًا شِتْويًّا.
ما الَّذي اتَّفَقَ عَلَيْهِ خالِدٌ ويوسُفُ بَعْدَ التَّسَوُّقِ؟
اتَّفَقا عَلى اللَّعِبِ مَعًا في المَلْعَبِ القَريبِ يَوْمَ الجُمُعةِ القادِمِ.
مَتى ذَهَبَ خالِدٌ ويوسُفُ لِلتَّسَوُّقِ؟
في عُطْلةِ نِهايةِ الأُسْبوعِ.
عَمَّ تَحَدَّثَ خالِدٌ ويوسُفُ؟
تَحَدَّثا عَنْ هِواياتِهِما المُفَضَّلةِ.
خالِدٌ اشْتَرى حِذاءً لِلَعِبِ كُرةِ القَدَمِ. (صَحّ / خَطَأ)
صَحّ ✓
خالِدٌ ويوسُفُ تَناوَلا الطَّعامَ خارِجَ المَرْكَزِ التِّجاريِّ. (صَحّ / خَطَأ)
خَطَأ ✗: جَلَسا في مَطْعَمٍ داخِلَ المَرْكَزِ.

9. التعبير الكتابي — writing models

a) Complete the dialogue (in the clothes shop)

خالِد: السَّلامُ عَلَيْكُمْ يا راشِدُ، كَيْفَ حالُكَ يا صَديقي؟
راشِد: وعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلامُ، أَنا بِخَيْرٍ والحَمْدُ لِلّهِ، وأَنْتَ؟
خالِد: هذا القَميصُ رائِعٌ! مِنْ أَيْنَ اشْتَرَيْتَهُ؟
راشِد: اشْتَرَيْتُهُ مِنْ ماكْس في مول الإماراتِ.
خالِد: بِكَمِ اشْتَرَيْتَهُ؟
راشِد: اشْتَرَيْتُهُ بِخَمْسينَ دِرْهَمًا.
خالِد: ما خامَتُهُ؟ وأَيْنَ صُنِعَ؟
راشِد: خامَتُهُ مِنَ القُطْنِ، وصُنِعَ في الهِنْدِ.
خالِد: هَلْ توجَدُ تَخْفيضاتٌ في المَتْجَرِ؟
راشِد: نَعَمْ، توجَدُ تَخْفيضاتٌ سَبْعونَ بِالمِئةِ.
خالِد: ما رَأْيُكَ في الأَسْعارِ هُناكَ؟
راشِد: في رَأْيي الأَسْعارُ مُناسِبةٌ وجَيِّدةٌ.
خالِد: شُكْرًا جَزيلًا يا راشِدُ، مَعَ السَّلامةِ.
راشِد: عَفْوًا، إلى اللِّقاءِ يا خالِدُ.
Answer exactly what the line before asks: مِنْ أَيْنَ → shop/mall; بِكَمْ → price + دِرْهَمًا; ما خامَتُهُ → القُطْن / الحَرير / الصّوف; أَيْنَ صُنِعَ → صُنِعَ في …; هَلْ → نَعَمْ / لا; ما رَأْيُكَ → في رَأْيي ….

b) Describe the picture (at least 3 lines + your opinion)

في الصّورةِ أَرى أُسْرةً في دُكّانِ المَلابِسِ. الأَبُ يَلْبَسُ كَنْدورةً بَيْضاءَ، والأُمُّ تَلْبَسُ عَباءةً سَوْداءَ. البِنْتُ تَخْتارُ فُسْتانًا وَرْديًّا جَميلًا، والوَلَدُ يَقيسُ قَميصًا أَزْرَقَ. في الدُّكّانِ مَلابِسُ كَثيرةٌ وأَلْوانٌ رائِعةٌ. في رَأْيي هذا الدُّكّانُ مُرَتَّبٌ ونَظيفٌ. ما أَجْمَلَ هذِهِ المَلابِسَ!

Formula: في الصّورةِ أَرى … + who is wearing what (colour + adjective after the noun) + the place + في رَأْيي … + one ما أَجْمَلَ …!

c) A situation that happened to you in a clothes shop (3+ lines)

في الأُسْبوعِ الماضي ذَهَبْتُ مَعَ أَبي إلى دُكّانِ المَلابِسِ لِأَشْتَرِيَ قَميصًا لِلْمَدْرَسةِ. أَعْجَبَني قَميصٌ أَبْيَضُ، لكِنَّهُ كانَ ضَيِّقًا. طَلَبْتُ مِنَ البائِعِ مَقاسًا أَكْبَرَ، فَأَحْضَرَهُ بِسُرْعةٍ. كانَ القَميصُ مُريحًا وسِعْرُهُ مُناسِبًا، فَاشْتَرَيْتُهُ وشَكَرْتُ البائِعَ.

d) A tweet about the clothes shop

زُرْتُ اليَوْمَ دُكّانَ "الأَناقة" في دُبَيّ 👕👗 مَلابِسُ جَميلةٌ وأَسْعارٌ مُناسِبةٌ وتَخْفيضاتٌ ٥٠٪! ما أَرْوَعَ قِسْمَ المَلابِسِ الرِّياضيّةِ! أَنْصَحُكُمْ بِزِيارَتِهِ. #دكان_الملابس #تسوق

e) Poster for your own clothes shop

It must have: shop name, pictures / drawings of clothes, a short slogan, and prices or discounts.

دُكّانُ النُّجومِ لِلْمَلابِسِ ⭐
"اِلْبَسْ أَناقَتَكَ … بِأَقَلِّ سِعْرٍ!"
👕 قَميصٌ قُطْنيٌّ: ٤٠ دِرْهَمًا   👖 بِنْطالٌ: ٦٠ دِرْهَمًا   👗 فُسْتانٌ: ٨٠ دِرْهَمًا
🔥 تَخْفيضاتٌ ٣٠٪ عَلى المَلابِسِ الصَّيْفيّةِ!
📍 دُبَيّ – مول الإماراتِ

f) Narrative text: a shopping trip (with whom, what you saw, what you bought, how you felt)

في يَوْمِ السَّبْتِ ذَهَبْتُ مَعَ أُسْرَتي إلى مول الإماراتِ لِشِراءِ بَعْضِ المَلابِسِ. شاهَدْنا مَحَلّاتٍ كَثيرةً ومَلابِسَ بِأَلْوانٍ جَميلةٍ. اشْتَرى أَبي بَدْلةً أَنيقةً، واشْتَرَتْ أُمّي عَباءةً سَوْداءَ، واخْتارَتْ أُخْتي فُسْتانًا وَرْديًّا. أَمّا أَنا فَاشْتَرَيْتُ قَميصًا رِياضيًّا وحِذاءً مُريحًا. أَعْجَبَتْني الأَلْوانُ كَثيرًا، لكِنْ في رَأْيي كانَتِ الأَسْعارُ مُرْتَفِعةً قَليلًا لِأَنَّهُ لا توجَدُ تَخْفيضاتٌ. في النِّهايةِ شَعَرْتُ بِالسَّعادةِ لِأَنَّنا قَضَيْنا يَوْمًا مُمْتِعًا مَعًا. ما أَجْمَلَ التَّسَوُّقَ مَعَ العائِلةِ!

g) Comparison: clothes in the UAE and my country (use تعجب + opinion words)

في الإماراتِ يَلْبَسُ الرِّجالُ الكَنْدورةَ البَيْضاءَ، وتَلْبَسُ النِّساءُ العَباءةَ السَّوْداءَ. ما أَجْمَلَ الكَنْدورةَ في اليَوْمِ الوَطَنيِّ! أَمّا في بَلَدي الهِنْدِ، فَيَلْبَسُ الرِّجالُ الكورْتا، وتَلْبَسُ النِّساءُ السّاري المُلَوَّنَ. ما أَرْوَعَ أَلْوانَ السّاري! المَلابِسُ في البَلَدَيْنِ خَفيفةٌ لِأَنَّ الجَوَّ حارٌّ. أَعْجَبَتْني الكَنْدورةُ لِأَنَّها مُريحةٌ، ولَمْ تُعْجِبْني الأَسْعارُ المُرْتَفِعةُ في بَعْضِ المولاتِ. في رَأْيي لِكُلِّ بَلَدٍ مَلابِسُ جَميلةٌ، وأُوافِقُ عَلى أَنَّ المَلابِسَ التَّقْليديّةَ تَحْكي ثَقافةَ الشَّعْبِ.
Checklist for writing marks: connectors (و، ثُمَّ، لكِنْ، بَيْنَما، أَمّا … فَـ، لِأَنَّ), adjectives after nouns, one ما أَجْمَلَ …!, opinion words (أَعْجَبَني / لَمْ يُعْجِبْني / في رَأْيي / أُوافِقُ), and correct verb endings for each person.

✅ Quick check — EOU2

ما أَطْوَلَ بُرْجَ خَليفة! — what type?
أُسْلوب تَعَجُّب (ما + أفعل + !)
يَشْرَبُ راشِدٌ الحَليبَ كُلَّ صَباحٍ. — اسمية or فعلية?
جُمْلة فِعْليّة (starts with the verb يَشْرَبُ)
مِنْ وِجْهةِ نَظَري مول الإماراتِ أَجْمَلُ مِنْ دُبَيّ مول. — what type?
عِبارة رَأْي
Make it feminine: راشِدٌ يَلْعَبُ مَعَ صَديقِهِ.
فاطِمةُ تَلْعَبُ مَعَ صَديقَتِها.
Odd one out: يَلْعَبُ – جَميلة – يَذْهَبُ – يُمارِسُ
جَميلة (adjective)
Correct it: أُخْتي تَشْتَري طَويل عَباءة.
أُخْتي تَشْتَري عَباءةً طَويلةً.
Make it negative: يَذْهَبُ راشِدٌ إلى المول.
لا يَذْهَبُ راشِدٌ إلى المول.
Make a تعجب: السّوقُ كَبيرٌ.
ما أَكْبَرَ السّوقَ!
Choose the question word: …… حالُكَ؟
كَيْفَ حالُكَ؟

📽️ Revision: Grammar & Phrases

1. Negation – النَّفْي

a) Present tense → لا + present verb

Just put لا in front. The verb does not change.

PositiveNegativeEnglish
أَلْبَسُ مِعْطَفاً.لا أَلْبَسُ مِعْطَفاً.I (don't) wear a coat.
يَلْبَسُ أَخي الكَنْدورة.لا يَلْبَسُ أَخي الكَنْدورة.My brother (doesn't) wear the kandura.
تُحِبُّ سارة اللَّوْن الأَسْوَد.لا تُحِبُّ سارة اللَّوْن الأَسْوَد.Sara (doesn't) like black.

b) Past tense → لَمْ + present verb (most used in school) or ما + past verb

With لَمْ you switch to the present form of the verb, but the meaning becomes past. With ما you keep the past verb.

Positive (past)Negative with لمNegative with ماEnglish
لَبِسْتُلَمْ أَلْبَسْما لَبِسْتُI wore → I didn't wear
لَبِسْتَ / لَبِسْتِلَمْ تَلْبَسْ / لَمْ تَلْبَسيما لَبِسْتَ / ما لَبِسْتِyou (m / f) didn't wear
لَبِسَلَمْ يَلْبَسْما لَبِسَhe didn't wear
لَبِسَتْلَمْ تَلْبَسْما لَبِسَتْshe didn't wear
لَبِسْنالَمْ نَلْبَسْما لَبِسْناwe didn't wear
لَبِسوالَمْ يَلْبَسواما لَبِسواthey didn't wear
Watch out after لم:
• The last letter gets a sukūn: لَمْ أَذْهَبْ (I didn't go).
• Verbs ending in ى / ي lose that letter: اِشْتَرى ← لَمْ يَشْتَرِ (he didn't buy).
• "They" loses the ن: يَلْبَسونَ ← لَمْ يَلْبَسوا.
• Never use لا with a past verb.

c) "Is not" (no verb) → لَيْسَ / لَيْسَتْ

القَميصُ لَيْسَ غالِياً. The shirt is not expensive. • التَّنّورةُ لَيْسَتْ طَويلةً. The skirt is not long.

✏️ Practice: make it negative

لَمْ أَلْبَسِ الكَنْدورةَ أَمْس. / ما لَبِسْتُ الكَنْدورةَ أَمْس.

اِشْتَرى أَبي حِذاءً جَديداً.

لَمْ يَشْتَرِ أَبي حِذاءً جَديداً. (ى drops after لم)

ذَهَبْنا إلى السّوق.

لَمْ نَذْهَبْ إلى السّوق.

تَلْبَسُ أُمّي عَباءةً سَوْداء.

لا تَلْبَسُ أُمّي عَباءةً سَوْداء.

الفُسْتانُ قَصيرٌ.

الفُسْتانُ لَيْسَ قَصيراً.

📽️ Revision: Colours & Agreement

2. Adjectives – الصِّفة والمَوْصوف

An adjective copies its noun in 3 ways:

  1. Position: after the noun → ثَوْبٌ طَويلٌ (a long robe).
  2. Gender: feminine noun → feminine adjective → عَباءةٌ سَوْداءُ, كَنْزةٌ جَميلةٌ.
  3. "The": if the noun has ال, so does the adjective → الكَنْدورةُ البَيْضاءُ (the white kandura).

➕ Plurals of things take a feminine singular adjective: مَلابِسُ تَقْليديّةٌ (traditional clothes), الأَحْذِيةُ السَّوْداءُ. Plurals of people take a plural adjective: طُلّابٌ جُدُدٌ (new students).

أَزْرَقزَرْقاءblue
أَخْضَرخَضْراءgreen
أَصْفَرصَفْراءyellow
أَسْوَدسَوْداءblack
أَبْيَضبَيْضاءwhite

بَنَفْسَجيّبَنَفْسَجيّةpurple
ذَهَبيّذَهَبيّةgold
Colours like أَحْمَر have their own feminine pattern (فَعْلاء: حَمْراء). Colours ending in ـيّ just add ة: بُنّيّ ← بُنّيّة.

4. Expressing preference – التَّعْبير عَنِ التَّفْضيل

ArabicEnglish
أُحِبُّ … / لا أُحِبُّ …I like … / I don't like …
أُفَضِّلُ … عَلى …I prefer … to (over) …
أُحِبُّ … أَكْثَرَ مِنْ …I like … more than …
يُعْجِبُني … / تُعْجِبُني …I like (m / f thing)
لَوْني المُفَضَّلُ هُوَ …My favourite colour is …
مَلابِسي المُفَضَّلةُ هِيَ …My favourite clothes are …
في رَأْيي …In my opinion …

Compare with أَفْعَل مِنْ (more … than)

جَميل ← أَجْمَلُ مِنْ more beautiful than • خَفيف ← أَخَفُّ مِنْ lighter than • رَخيص ← أَرْخَصُ مِنْ cheaper than • غالٍ ← أَغْلى مِنْ more expensive than • طَويل ← أَطْوَلُ مِنْ longer than • مُريح ← أَكْثَرُ راحةً مِنْ more comfortable than

أُفَضِّلُ الكَنْدورةَ عَلى البِنْطالِ لِأَنَّها أَخَفُّ وأَكْثَرُ راحةً.
لَوْني المُفَضَّلُ هُوَ الأَزْرَقُ، لِذلِكَ أُحِبُّ القُمْصانَ الزَّرْقاءَ.
لا أُحِبُّ المِعْطَفَ لِأَنَّهُ ثَقيلٌ.

I prefer the kandura to trousers because it is lighter and more comfortable. • My favourite colour is blue, so I like blue shirts. • I don't like the coat because it is heavy.

Always give a reason: preference + لِأَنَّ + adjective = full marks sentence.
📽️ Revision: Reading practice

1. How to answer reading questions

  1. Read the questions first so you know what to look for.
  2. First read: the general idea (who? where? what?). Second read: details — clothes, colours, reasons.
  3. "Why" questions → look for لِأَنَّ or لِذلِكَ in the text.
  4. Answer in a full sentence using words from the question.
  5. True/false: if false, correct it using the text.

Question words

ماذا؟ / ما؟what?كَيْفَ؟how?
أَيْنَ؟where?كَمْ؟ / بِكَمْ؟how many? / how much (price)?
مَتى؟when?هَلْ؟yes/no question
ما لَوْنُ …؟what colour is …?اِسْتَخْرِجْ مِنَ النَّصّfind in the text
صَحّ أَمْ خَطَأtrue or falseضِدّ / جَمْع / مُفْرَدopposite / plural / singular

2. Main passage – الملابس حول العالم

لِكُلِّ بَلَدٍ مَلابِسُ تَقْليديّةٌ خاصّةٌ بِهِ. في الإماراتِ يَلْبَسُ الرِّجالُ الكَنْدورةَ البَيْضاءَ، وهِيَ ثَوْبٌ طَويلٌ وواسِعٌ، ويَلْبَسونَ عَلى رُؤوسِهِمُ الغُتْرةَ والعِقالَ. وتَلْبَسُ النِّساءُ العَباءةَ السَّوْداءَ والشَّيْلةَ. هذِهِ المَلابِسُ خَفيفةٌ ومُريحةٌ لِأَنَّ الجَوَّ حارٌّ في الصَّيْفِ.
في اليابانِ يَلْبَسُ النّاسُ الكيمونو في الحَفَلاتِ والمُناسَباتِ. الكيمونو ثَوْبٌ طَويلٌ مِنَ الحَريرِ، ولَهُ أَكْمامٌ واسِعةٌ وأَلْوانٌ جَميلةٌ.
أَمّا في الهِنْدِ، فَتَلْبَسُ النِّساءُ السّاري، وهُوَ قِطْعةُ قُماشٍ طَويلةٌ ومُلَوَّنةٌ، ويَلْبَسُ الرِّجالُ الكورْتا، وهِيَ قَميصٌ طَويلٌ مِنَ القُطْنِ.
وفي اسْكُتْلَنْدا يَلْبَسُ الرِّجالُ التَّنّورةَ الاسْكُتْلَنْديّةَ في المُناسَباتِ، وهِيَ مِنَ الصّوفِ لِأَنَّ الجَوَّ بارِدٌ هُناكَ.
المَلابِسُ التَّقْليديّةُ تَحْكي قِصّةَ كُلِّ شَعْبٍ وثَقافَتِهِ.
Show English translation

Every country has its own traditional clothes. In the UAE men wear the white kandura, a long loose robe, and on their heads they wear the ghutra and the ʿiqāl. Women wear the black abaya and the shayla. These clothes are light and comfortable because the weather is hot in summer. In Japan people wear the kimono at parties and special occasions. The kimono is a long silk robe with wide sleeves and beautiful colours. As for India, women wear the sari, a long colourful piece of cloth, and men wear the kurta, a long cotton shirt. In Scotland men wear the kilt at special occasions; it is made of wool because the weather is cold there. Traditional clothes tell the story of every people and their culture.

A. Answer the questions

ماذا يَلْبَسُ الرِّجالُ في الإماراتِ؟

يَلْبَسُ الرِّجالُ في الإماراتِ الكَنْدورةَ البَيْضاءَ والغُتْرةَ والعِقالَ.

لِماذا المَلابِسُ في الإماراتِ خَفيفةٌ؟

لِأَنَّ الجَوَّ حارٌّ في الصَّيْفِ.

مِنْ أَيِّ قُماشٍ الكيمونو؟

الكيمونو مِنَ الحَريرِ.

مَتى يَلْبَسُ اليابانيّونَ الكيمونو؟

في الحَفَلاتِ والمُناسَباتِ.

لِماذا التَّنّورةُ الاسْكُتْلَنْديّةُ مِنَ الصّوفِ؟

لِأَنَّ الجَوَّ بارِدٌ في اسْكُتْلَنْدا.

السّاري قِطْعةُ قُماشٍ قَصيرةٌ.

✅ صَحّ

3. Unseen passage practice A

اسمي ليلى. في الصباح كان الجو بارداً، لذلك لبستُ كنزة صفراء وسترة زرقاء. لبست أيضاً تنورة سوداء وجوارب بيضاء. أخي عمر لبس معطفاً بنياً ووشاحاً أحمر. ثم ذهبنا إلى المدرسة بالحافلة.

My name is Layla. In the morning the weather was cold, so I wore a yellow sweater and a blue jacket. I also wore a black skirt and white socks. My brother Omar wore a brown coat and a red scarf. Then we went to school by bus.

1. Why did Layla wear a sweater and jacket?

لأن الجو كان بارداً. (Because the weather was cold.)

2. What colour was Omar's scarf?

أحمر (red)

3. Why is it سترة زرقاء but معطفاً بنياً?

سترة is feminine (ends in ة), so it takes the feminine colour زرقاء; معطف is masculine, so it takes بني.

4. How did they go to school?

بالحافلة (by bus)

4. Unseen passage practice B

ذهبت مريم مع أمها إلى السوق لشراء ملابس العيد. اشترت فستاناً أخضر وحذاءً أبيض. أرادت قبعة وردية، لكنها كانت غالية جداً، لذلك اشترت وشاحاً وردياً.

Maryam went with her mother to the market to buy Eid clothes. She bought a green dress and white shoes. She wanted a pink hat, but it was very expensive, so she bought a pink scarf.

1. Why did Maryam go to the market?

To buy Eid clothes (لشراء ملابس العيد).

2. Why didn't she buy the pink hat?

لأنها كانت غالية جداً. (Because it was very expensive.)

3. Find a feminine colour in the passage and the noun it describes.

قبعة وردية (a pink hat)

5. 3asafeer read-aloud tips (formative)

  • Read slowly and follow the ḥarakāt (vowel marks: ـَ a, ـِ i, ـُ u).
  • Pause at full stops and commas; raise your voice at ؟ (question).
  • Don't stop at a hard word — sound it out letter by letter, then keep going.
  • After reading, the teacher asks questions: answer with a full sentence and words from the story.
  • Practise: read one 3asafeer story aloud every day for 5 minutes.
📽️ Revision: Writing a Paragraph

1. Describing my clothes and other people's clothes

she / my motherتَلْبَسُتَلْبَسُ أُمّي عَباءةً سَوْداءَ.
weنَلْبَسُنَلْبَسُ الزّيَّ المَدْرَسيَّ.
they (boys / girls)يَلْبَسونَ / يَلْبَسْنَيَلْبَسُ الطُّلّابُ… / تَلْبَسُ الطّالِباتُ…

Tip: when the verb comes before the people, it stays singular: يَلْبَسُ الطُّلّابُ (not يلبسون الطلاب).

Model answer

في يَوْمِ العيدِ نَلْبَسُ مَلابِسَ جَديدةً وجَميلةً. أَنا أَلْبَسُ كورْتا زَرْقاءَ طَويلةً مِنَ القُطْنِ وبِنْطالاً أَبْيَضَ، لِأَنَّ القُطْنَ خَفيفٌ والجَوَّ حارٌّ. وأَلْبَسُ أَيْضاً صَنْدَلاً بُنّيّاً.
يَلْبَسُ أَبي كَنْدورةً بَيْضاءَ واسِعةً، وتَلْبَسُ أُمّي ساري أَحْمَرَ مُلَوَّناً. أُخْتي الصَّغيرةُ تَلْبَسُ فُسْتاناً وَرْدِيّاً قَصيراً.
لا أُحِبُّ المَلابِسَ الضَّيِّقةَ لِأَنَّها غَيْرُ مُريحةٍ. في رَأْيي، أَجْمَلُ المَلابِسِ هِيَ المَلابِسُ التَّقْليديّةُ.
English translation

On Eid we wear new, beautiful clothes. I wear a long blue cotton kurta and white trousers, because cotton is light and the weather is hot. I also wear brown sandals. My father wears a loose white kandura and my mother wears a colourful red sari. My little sister wears a short pink dress. I don't like tight clothes because they are uncomfortable. In my opinion, the most beautiful clothes are traditional clothes.

✏️ Change the clothes and family members to match your family.

2. Comparison: clothes in my country vs the UAE

Comparison words

ArabicEnglish
أَمّا … فَـ …as for … (then) …
بَيْنَماwhile / whereas
مِثْلَlike (similar to)
يُشْبِهُ / تُشْبِهُresembles (m / f)
يَخْتَلِفُ عَنْ / تَخْتَلِفُ عَنْis different from
كِلاهُماboth of them
في بَلَدي … / في الإمارات …in my country … / in the UAE …
أَجْمَلُ مِنْ / أَخَفُّ مِنْmore beautiful than / lighter than

Plan (4 short paragraphs)

  1. Clothes in my country (men + women, colours, material, occasions).
  2. Clothes in the UAE.
  3. Similarities (مِثْلَ، كِلاهُما) and differences (بَيْنَما، أَمّا).
  4. Which I prefer and why.

Model answer (India → change to your country)

في بَلَدي الهِنْدِ يَلْبَسُ الرِّجالُ الكورْتا والبِنْطالَ، وتَلْبَسُ النِّساءُ السّاري المُلَوَّنَ. المَلابِسُ الهِنْدِيّةُ مُلَوَّنةٌ جِدّاً: حَمْراءُ وصَفْراءُ وخَضْراءُ.
أَمّا في الإماراتِ، فَيَلْبَسُ الرِّجالُ الكَنْدورةَ البَيْضاءَ والغُتْرةَ، وتَلْبَسُ النِّساءُ العَباءةَ السَّوْداءَ والشَّيْلةَ.
المَلابِسُ في البَلَدَيْنِ خَفيفةٌ وواسِعةٌ لِأَنَّ الجَوَّ حارٌّ، وكِلاهُما مِنَ القُطْنِ غالِباً. لكِنَّ المَلابِسَ في الهِنْدِ مُلَوَّنةٌ، بَيْنَما المَلابِسُ التَّقْليديّةُ في الإماراتِ بَيْضاءُ أَوْ سَوْداءُ.
أَنا أُفَضِّلُ الكورْتا عَلى البِنْطالِ لِأَنَّها أَكْثَرُ راحةً، وأُحِبُّ الكَنْدورةَ أَيْضاً لِأَنَّها بَسيطةٌ وجَميلةٌ.
English translation

In my country, India, men wear the kurta and trousers, and women wear the colourful sari. Indian clothes are very colourful: red, yellow and green. As for the UAE, men wear the white kandura and the ghutra, and women wear the black abaya and the shayla. Clothes in both countries are light and loose because the weather is hot, and both are usually made of cotton. But clothes in India are colourful, whereas traditional clothes in the UAE are white or black. I prefer the kurta to trousers because it is more comfortable, and I also like the kandura because it is simple and beautiful.

Before you hand in, check: (1) adjective after the noun, (2) feminine adjective with ة nouns and with plurals of things, (3) ال on both noun and adjective, (4) at least two لأنّ, (5) at least one negative sentence (لا / لم), (6) one preference sentence (أُفَضِّلُ … عَلى), (7) comparison words.
📝 Practice sheet: 15 fresh questions on this topic

1. Speaking: my school uniform and my classmates'

أَنا في الصَّفِّ السّابِعِ. أَلْبَسُ الزّيَّ المَدْرَسيَّ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. زِيّي قَميصٌ أَبْيَضُ وبِنْطالٌ رَماديٌّ، وأَلْبَسُ حِذاءً أَسْوَدَ وجَوارِبَ بَيْضاءَ.
زُمَلائي يَلْبَسونَ الزّيَّ نَفْسَهُ. البَناتُ يَلْبَسْنَ قَميصاً أَبْيَضَ وتَنّورةً رَماديّةً طَويلةً.
في يَوْمِ الرِّياضةِ نَلْبَسُ الزّيَّ الرِّياضيَّ وحِذاءً رِياضيّاً.
أُحِبُّ زِيّي المَدْرَسيَّ لِأَنَّهُ مُريحٌ، لكِنْ لا أُحِبُّ الحِذاءَ الأَسْوَدَ لِأَنَّهُ ثَقيلٌ.

I am in Grade 7. I wear the school uniform every day. My uniform is a white shirt and grey trousers, and I wear black shoes and white socks. My classmates wear the same uniform. The girls wear a white shirt and a long grey skirt. On sports day we wear the sports uniform and trainers. I like my uniform because it is comfortable, but I don't like the black shoes because they are heavy.

✏️ Change the colours to match your real uniform. Speak in short, clear sentences and include one negative and one preference.

Questions the teacher may ask

ما لَوْنُ قَميصِكَ؟

قَميصي أَبْيَضُ.

ماذا يَلْبَسُ زُمَلاؤُكَ؟

يَلْبَسُ زُمَلائي قَميصاً أَبْيَضَ وبِنْطالاً رَماديّاً.

هَلْ تُحِبُّ زِيَّكَ المَدْرَسيَّ؟ لِماذا؟

نَعَمْ، أُحِبُّهُ لِأَنَّهُ مُريحٌ.

ماذا تَلْبَسُ في يَوْمِ الرِّياضةِ؟

أَلْبَسُ الزّيَّ الرِّياضيَّ.

2. Listening tips

  • Read the questions before the audio starts and underline the question words.
  • Listen for: clothes, colours, numbers/prices, places, and لأنّ (the reason comes after it).
  • Write quick notes in English or short Arabic words while listening.
  • Second listening: check and fill gaps. Never leave an answer blank.

3. Writing a dialogue with the seller – حِوار مَعَ البائِع

Useful phrases

Seller – البائِعCustomer – الزَّبون
أَهْلاً وسَهْلاً! كَيْفَ أُساعِدُكَ؟أُريدُ أَنْ أَشْتَرِيَ …
أَيَّ لَوْنٍ تُفَضِّلُ؟أُفَضِّلُ اللَّوْنَ …
ما مَقاسُكَ؟مَقاسي صَغيرٌ / مُتَوَسِّطٌ / كَبيرٌ.
تَفَضَّلْ، هذا / هذِهِ …هَلْ عِنْدَكَ مَقاسٌ أَكْبَرُ / أَصْغَرُ؟
بِـ … دِرْهَماً.بِكَمْ هذا القَميصُ؟ / بِكَمْ هذِهِ العَباءةُ؟
عِنْدَنا لَوْنٌ آخَرُ.هذا غالٍ! هَلْ عِنْدَكَ شَيْءٌ أَرْخَصُ؟
شُكْراً لَكَ، مَعَ السَّلامة!سَآخُذُهُ (m) / سَآخُذُها (f). شُكْراً!

Model dialogue

البائِعُ: أَهْلاً وسَهْلاً! كَيْفَ أُساعِدُكَ؟
الزَّبونُ: أُريدُ أَنْ أَشْتَرِيَ قَميصاً لِلمَدْرَسةِ.
البائِعُ: أَيَّ لَوْنٍ تُفَضِّلُ؟
الزَّبونُ: أُفَضِّلُ اللَّوْنَ الأَبْيَضَ.
البائِعُ: ما مَقاسُكَ؟
الزَّبونُ: مَقاسي مُتَوَسِّطٌ.
البائِعُ: تَفَضَّلْ، هذا قَميصٌ أَبْيَضُ مِنَ القُطْنِ.
الزَّبونُ: هذا القَميصُ ضَيِّقٌ قَليلاً. هَلْ عِنْدَكَ مَقاسٌ أَكْبَرُ؟
البائِعُ: نَعَمْ، تَفَضَّلْ.
الزَّبونُ: بِكَمْ هذا القَميصُ؟
البائِعُ: بِسِتّينَ دِرْهَماً.
الزَّبونُ: هذا غالٍ! هَلْ عِنْدَكَ قَميصٌ أَرْخَصُ؟
البائِعُ: هذا بِأَرْبَعينَ دِرْهَماً، لكِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنَ القُطْنِ.
الزَّبونُ: لا، أُفَضِّلُ القَميصَ القُطْنيَّ لِأَنَّهُ مُريحٌ. سَآخُذُهُ.
البائِعُ: شُكْراً لَكَ. مَعَ السَّلامةِ!
الزَّبونُ: مَعَ السَّلامةِ.
English translation

Seller: Welcome! How can I help you? – Customer: I want to buy a shirt for school. – S: Which colour do you prefer? – C: I prefer white. – S: What is your size? – C: Medium. – S: Here you are, a white cotton shirt. – C: This shirt is a bit tight. Do you have a bigger size? – S: Yes, here you are. – C: How much is this shirt? – S: Sixty dirhams. – C: That's expensive! Do you have a cheaper shirt? – S: This one is forty dirhams, but it isn't cotton. – C: No, I prefer the cotton shirt because it is comfortable. I'll take it. – S: Thank you. Goodbye! – C: Goodbye.

To score high, your dialogue should include: greeting • item + colour + size • a price question • a negative (لَيْسَ / لا) • a preference with a reason • a polite ending. Put each speaker on a new line with a colon.

🎨 Enrichment: design an outfit inspired by a culture

  1. Choose a country (Japan, India, Korea, Scotland, Mexico, Egypt, UAE…).
  2. Research: what do men and women wear? Colours? Material? When is it worn?
  3. Design your own outfit inspired by it. Draw it, colour it and label each piece in Arabic with a correct adjective.
  4. Write 5–6 sentences to present it.

Sentence starters

ArabicEnglish
اِخْتَرْتُ بَلَدَ …I chose the country …
المَلابِسُ التَّقْليديّةُ في … هِيَ …The traditional clothes in … are …
يَلْبَسُ النّاسُ … في …People wear … at/in …
هُوَ / هِيَ مِنَ الحَريرِ / القُطْنِ / الصّوفِ.It is made of silk / cotton / wool.
صَمَّمْتُ زِيّاً جَديداً مُسْتَوْحىً مِنْ …I designed a new outfit inspired by …
أُحِبُّ تَصْميمي لِأَنَّهُ …I like my design because it is …

Model: Japan 🇯🇵

اِخْتَرْتُ اليابانَ. المَلابِسُ التَّقْليديّةُ في اليابانِ هِيَ الكيمونو. يَلْبَسُ النّاسُ الكيمونو في الحَفَلاتِ والأَعْيادِ. الكيمونو ثَوْبٌ طَويلٌ مِنَ الحَريرِ، ولَهُ أَكْمامٌ واسِعةٌ.
صَمَّمْتُ زِيّاً جَديداً مُسْتَوْحىً مِنَ الكيمونو: سُتْرةٌ حَمْراءُ قَصيرةٌ بِأَكْمامٍ واسِعةٍ، وبِنْطالٌ أَسْوَدُ واسِعٌ، وحِزامٌ ذَهَبيٌّ.
أُحِبُّ تَصْميمي لِأَنَّهُ جَميلٌ ومُريحٌ.

I chose Japan. The traditional clothes in Japan are the kimono. People wear the kimono at parties and festivals. The kimono is a long silk robe with wide sleeves. I designed a new outfit inspired by the kimono: a short red jacket with wide sleeves, loose black trousers and a gold belt. I like my design because it is beautiful and comfortable.

Poster checklist: country name + flag • picture of the real traditional clothes • your coloured design • Arabic labels with agreeing adjectives (سُتْرةٌ حَمْراءُ, حِزامٌ ذَهَبيٌّ) • your 5–6 sentences • neat title: المَلابِسُ حَوْلَ العالَم
⭐ Extra — beyond the Half Yearly syllabus. Helpful for higher marks in writing and speaking, but not required.

1. My / your / his / her (possessive endings)

EndingExampleEnglish
ـيقَميصيmy shirt
ـكَ / ـكِقَميصُكَ / قَميصُكِyour shirt (m / f)
ـهُ / ـهاقَميصُهُ / قَميصُهاhis / her shirt
ـنازِيُّناour uniform

With ة the ة becomes ت: تَنّورة ← تَنّورَتي (my skirt).

2. The dual – المُثَنّى (two things)

Add ـانِ: قَميص ← قَميصانِ (two shirts) • with ة → ـتانِ: تَنّورة ← تَنّورَتانِ. The adjective is dual too: قَميصانِ أَبْيَضانِ.

3. Future negation – لَنْ

سَأَلْبَسُ I will wear → لَنْ أَلْبَسَ I will not wear. (لن + present verb ending in -a.)

4. Prices: tens of dirhams

NumberArabicNumberArabic
10عَشَرة دَراهِم60سِتّونَ دِرْهَماً
20عِشْرونَ دِرْهَماً70سَبْعونَ دِرْهَماً
30ثَلاثونَ دِرْهَماً80ثَمانونَ دِرْهَماً
40أَرْبَعونَ دِرْهَماً90تِسْعونَ دِرْهَماً
50خَمْسونَ دِرْهَماً100مِئةُ دِرْهَمٍ

After "at / for" (بِـ) the ending changes to -īna: بِسِتّينَ دِرْهَماً.

✅ Revision checklist

  • I can conjugate -er, -ir and -re verbs in the présent.
  • I know the présent of être, avoir, aller, faire, prendre, venir, pouvoir, vouloir, devoir, savoir, mettre, dire, lire, écrire, boire.
  • I can use quel / quelle / quels / quelles and write a question for an answer.
  • I can make the futur proche (aller + infinitive).
  • I can give orders with the impératif — including SAVE (savoir, avoir, vouloir, être).
  • I can conjugate reflexive verbs (je me lève…) and describe my day.
  • I can make sentences negative with ne … pas / jamais / plus / rien / personne.
  • I can use mon / ma / mes … and ce / cet / cette / ces.
  • I know the vocabulary of Bonne Journée and La banque.
  • I can answer all 15 Culture & Civilisation questions in full sentences.
📝 Practice sheet: 15 fresh questions on this topic

1. How to answer reading questions

  1. Read the questions first so you know what to look for.
  2. Read the text once for the general idea, then again slowly.
  3. Underline key words from the question in the text (names, times, places).
  4. Answer in a full sentence, using words from the text but changing the person if needed.
TaskHow to do itExample
Répondez aux questionsFull sentence. Change je → il/elle if the text is in the first person.À quelle heure se lève Léa ? → Elle se lève à sept heures.
Vrai ou fauxWrite VRAI or FAUX and copy the sentence from the text that proves it.Léa prend le bus. → FAUX : « Elle va à l'école à pied. »
Trouvez dans le texteCopy the exact word or phrase — no changes.Trouvez un verbe pronominal. → se brosse
Question words: qui (who) · que / qu'est-ce que (what) · où (where) · quand (when) · à quelle heure (at what time) · comment (how) · pourquoi → parce que (why → because) · combien (how much / many) · quel / quelle (which / what)

2. Practice text 1 — Une journée de Léa

Bonjour ! Je m'appelle Léa et j'ai douze ans. Pendant la semaine, je me réveille à six heures et demie. D'abord, je me lève et je me douche. Ensuite, je m'habille et je prends mon petit-déjeuner avec mon frère Hugo : nous mangeons des tartines et nous buvons du jus d'orange. Je vais à l'école à pied parce que l'école est près de chez moi. Les cours commencent à huit heures. À midi, je déjeune à la cantine avec mes amies. L'après-midi, j'ai maths et français. Je rentre à la maison à quatre heures. Le soir, je fais mes devoirs, puis je regarde la télé. Je ne me couche jamais après dix heures !

Répondez aux questions

1. À quelle heure Léa se réveille-t-elle ?

Elle se réveille à six heures et demie.

2. Qu'est-ce qu'elle mange au petit-déjeuner ?

Elle mange des tartines (et elle boit du jus d'orange).

3. Comment va-t-elle à l'école ? Pourquoi ?

Elle va à l'école à pied parce que l'école est près de chez elle.

4. Où déjeune-t-elle ?

Elle déjeune à la cantine (avec ses amies).

Vrai ou faux ? Justifiez.

5. Léa a treize ans.

FAUX : « j'ai douze ans ».

6. Les cours commencent à huit heures.

VRAI : « Les cours commencent à huit heures ».

7. Léa se couche souvent à onze heures.

FAUX : « Je ne me couche jamais après dix heures ».

Trouvez dans le texte

8. Deux verbes pronominaux

je me réveille, je me lève, je me douche, je m'habille, je me couche (any two)

9. Un adjectif possessif

mon (petit-déjeuner / frère), mes (amies / devoirs)

10. Une phrase négative

Je ne me couche jamais après dix heures.

11. Deux mots de séquence

d'abord, ensuite, puis

3. Practice text 2 — À la banque

Samedi matin, M. Martin va à la banque près de la poste. Il veut ouvrir un compte pour son fils Paul. Au guichet, l'employée dit : « Bonjour monsieur, je peux vous aider ? » M. Martin répond : « Oui, je voudrais ouvrir un compte pour mon fils, s'il vous plaît. » L'employée demande : « Quel âge a votre fils ? » — « Il a quatorze ans. » — « Très bien. Remplissez ce formulaire et signez ici, s'il vous plaît. Avez-vous une pièce d'identité ? » M. Martin donne son passeport. Ensuite, il veut retirer de l'argent : il utilise sa carte bancaire au distributeur. Paul est content : il va mettre son argent de poche sur son nouveau compte !

1. Pourquoi M. Martin va-t-il à la banque ?

Il veut ouvrir un compte pour son fils (Paul).

2. Quel âge a Paul ?

Il a quatorze ans.

3. Vrai ou faux : M. Martin donne sa carte d'identité. Justifiez.

FAUX : « M. Martin donne son passeport ».

4. Comment retire-t-il de l'argent ?

Il utilise sa carte bancaire au distributeur.

5. Trouvez un verbe à l'impératif.

Remplissez / signez

6. Trouvez un adjectif interrogatif.

Quel (âge)

7. Trouvez un adjectif démonstratif.

ce (formulaire)

8. Trouvez une phrase au futur proche.

Il va mettre son argent de poche sur son nouveau compte.

📝 Practice sheet: 15 fresh questions on this topic

1. Décrivez votre journée quotidienne

Write about your typical day in the présent, in order, using reflexive verbs, times and sequence words.

Use…Examples
Sequence wordsd'abord (first) · ensuite / puis (then) · après (after) · plus tard (later) · enfin / finalement (finally)
Timeà sept heures · à midi · le matin · l'après-midi · le soir · tous les jours · d'habitude
Reflexive verbsje me réveille · je me lève · je me lave · je me douche · je me brosse les dents · je m'habille · je me couche
Other verbsje prends le petit-déjeuner · je vais à l'école · je déjeune · je rentre · je fais mes devoirs · je dîne · je regarde la télé
Connectors & opinionet · mais · parce que · car · alors · J'aime… / Je n'aime pas… parce que c'est…
Model answer:
D'habitude, je me réveille à six heures et quart. D'abord, je me lève et je me douche. Ensuite, je m'habille et je me brosse les dents. À sept heures, je prends mon petit-déjeuner : je mange des céréales et je bois du lait. Puis, je vais à l'école en bus avec ma sœur. Les cours commencent à sept heures et demie. À midi, je déjeune avec mes amis. J'aime les maths parce que c'est intéressant, mais je n'aime pas l'histoire. Je rentre à la maison à deux heures et demie. L'après-midi, je fais mes devoirs et je joue au foot. Le soir, je dîne avec ma famille. Enfin, je me couche à neuf heures et demie.
Checklist for full marks: ✅ at least 6 reflexive verbs · ✅ 4+ times · ✅ 4+ sequence words · ✅ one opinion with parce que · ✅ one negative · ✅ correct verb endings · ✅ capital letters and full stops.

2. Mettez le dialogue en ordre et récrivez (max. 7 lines)

In the exam you get a short dialogue (up to 7 lines) in a mixed-up order. You must find the right order and rewrite the whole dialogue correctly.

Method — 5 steps

  1. Read all the lines first. Work out who is talking (e.g. an employé and a client) and where (bank, phone, home, school).
  2. Find the opening line — a greeting or a call: Bonjour…, Salut…, Allô…, Excuse-moi…
  3. Find the closing line — a goodbye: Au revoir, Bonne journée, À samedi, À plus tard, Merci beaucoup.
  4. Match every question with its answer (see the table). A question is always followed by its answer.
  5. Check the speakers alternate (A, B, A, B…) and that each line makes sense after the one before. Then rewrite it in full.
If a line has……the next line probably has
Est-ce que… ? / Vous avez… ? / Tu veux… ?Oui, … / Non, …
Combien… ?a number / a price (cent dirhams, dix euros)
À quelle heure… ?a time (à sept heures et demie)
Où… ?a place (devant la banque, sur ta chaise)
Pourquoi… ?Parce que…
Comment… ?how (en bus, à pied, bien)
Qu'est-ce que… ?an action or a thing (je vais…, je voudrais…)
an order / request (Remplissez…, Lève-toi…)Voilà / D'accord / J'arrive
Exam tips: write the order clearly (e.g. b → d → g → a…) and rewrite the dialogue · put the speaker's name and a colon before each line · copy every word exactly — don't change spellings, accents or punctuation · the first line is almost never the one with "Merci" or "Au revoir".

Dialogue 1: 🏦 À la banque — ouvrir un compte (7 lines)

Tap the lines in the right order — the number shows where you put each one.

Employé : Merci. Remplissez ce formulaire et signez ici.

3. Complétez le texte à l'aide des mots donnés

Method: read the whole text first · look at the word just before and after the gap · decide the type of word needed (verb? noun? adjective?) · check gender and plural (une → feminine, les → plural) · cross off each word as you use it.

Mots : lève · banque · petit-déjeuner · argent · couche · compte · prends · distributeur

Le matin, je me (1) ______ à sept heures. Je (2) ______ mon (3) ______ dans la cuisine. Samedi, je vais à la (4) ______ avec mon père. Il veut retirer de l'(5) ______ au (6) ______. Moi, je voudrais ouvrir un (7) ______. Le soir, je me (8) ______ à dix heures.

Answers

1 lève · 2 prends · 3 petit-déjeuner · 4 banque · 5 argent · 6 distributeur · 7 compte · 8 couche

1. Regular verbs in the présent (-ER / -IR / -RE)

Remove the ending (-er, -ir, -re) to get the stem, then add the endings:

-ER · parler-IR · finir-RE · vendre

3. Futur proche — "going to"

aller (présent) + infinitive
Je vais manger. Nous allons regarder un film. Ils vont jouer.
PersonallerExample
jevaisJe vais faire mes devoirs.
tuvasTu vas aller à la banque.
il / ellevaElle va ouvrir un compte.
nousallonsNous allons voyager.
vousallezVous allez retirer de l'argent.
ils / ellesvontIls vont se coucher tard.

Negative: ne … pas goes around aller: Je ne vais pas sortir. Reflexive: the pronoun stays with the infinitive: Je vais me lever.

Time words: demain, ce soir, ce week-end, la semaine prochaine, l'année prochaine, bientôt.

Put into futur proche: Je mange.

Je vais manger.

Put into futur proche: Nous nous levons.

Nous allons nous lever.

Negative: Il va sortir.

Il ne va pas sortir.

4. L'impératif

The impératif (with SAVE) now has its own tab → 📣 L'impératif.

5. Verbes pronominaux (reflexive verbs)

The action is done to yourself, so there's an extra pronoun: me, te, se, nous, vous, se.

se lavers'habiller (vowel → m', t', s')
je me laveje m'habille
tu te lavestu t'habilles
il / elle se laveil / elle s'habille
nous nous lavonsnous nous habillons
vous vous lavezvous vous habillez
ils / elles se laventils / elles s'habillent

Daily-routine verbs: se réveiller (wake up) · se lever (get up — je me lève) · se laver · se doucher · se brosser les dents / les cheveux · s'habiller · se coiffer · se dépêcher (hurry) · se reposer · se coucher · s'amuser · s'appeler (je m'appelle).

Negative: ne goes before the pronoun, pas after the verb: Je ne me lève pas tôt.

Conjugate: nous (se réveiller)

nous nous réveillons

Conjugate: elle (s'habiller)

elle s'habille

Make negative: Tu te couches tard.

Tu ne te couches pas tard.

📣 L'impératif is in your grammar section (Section C) — know the regular forms, SAVE, the negative and reflexive verbs.

1. How to make the impératif

Use the tu, nous or vous form of the présent, without the subject.

tunous (let's…)vous
parlerParle !Parlons !Parlez !
finirFinis !Finissons !Finissez !
attendreAttends !Attendons !Attendez !
allerVa !Allons !Allez !
Rule: -er verbs (and aller) drop the -s in the tu form: tu écoutes → Écoute !

The 4 irregular ones — remember SAVE

Verbtunousvous
SsavoirSacheSachonsSachez
AavoirAieAyonsAyez
VvouloirVeuilleVeuillonsVeuillez
EêtreSoisSoyonsSoyez

Negative: Ne parle pas ! · N'oubliez pas ! · Ne sois pas en retard !
Reflexive: positive → pronoun after with a hyphen (te → toi): Lève-toi ! Levons-nous ! Levez-vous ! · negative → back in front: Ne te lève pas !

Give the vous imperative of être.

Soyez !

Make negative: Mange !

Ne mange pas !

Imperative (tu) of se dépêcher

Dépêche-toi !

2. When do we use it?

UseExampleEnglish
OrdersFerme la porte !Close the door!
AdviceBois de l'eau !Drink water!
Instructions (exam questions!)Répondez aux questions. Mettez au négatif. Complétez le texte.Answer… Make negative… Complete…
Suggestions with nousAllons au parc !Let's go to the park!
Polite requests (vous)Remplissez ce formulaire, s'il vous plaît.Fill in this form, please.
Who am I talking to? one friend / family → tu form · a teacher, adult, or several people → vous form · "let's" → nous form.

3. More irregular forms to know

Verbtunousvous
allerVaAllonsAllez
faireFaisFaisonsFaites
prendrePrendsPrenonsPrenez
venirViensVenonsVenez
direDisDisonsDites
mettreMetsMettonsMettez
ouvrir (-er pattern!)OuvreOuvronsOuvrez

4. Common mistakes

  • ❌ Tu écoute ! / Écoutes ! → ✅ Écoute ! (no subject, no -s for -er verbs)
  • ❌ Soit gentil ! → ✅ Sois gentil ! (être → sois)
  • ❌ Lève-te ! → ✅ Lève-toi ! (te → toi after the verb)
  • ❌ Ne lève-toi pas ! → ✅ Ne te lève pas !
  • ✅ Before y / en the -s comes back: Vas-y ! (Go on!)

1. Adjectifs interrogatifs — quel, quelle, quels, quelles

Quel means which / what and must agree with the noun after it:

SingularPlural
MasculineQuel âge as-tu ?Quels sports aimes-tu ?
FeminineQuelle heure est-il ?Quelles matières préfères-tu ?

It also works before être: Quelle est ta couleur préférée ? Quel est ton numéro de compte ?

___ heure est-il ?

Quelle (heure is feminine)

___ livres lis-tu ?

___ est ton nom ?

2. Asking questions — 3 ways

WayHowExample
1 · IntonationStatement + voice goes upTu aimes le chocolat ?
2 · Est-ce queEst-ce que + statementEst-ce que tu aimes le chocolat ?
3 · InversionVerb–subject with a hyphenAimes-tu le chocolat ? (il/elle + vowel → -t-: Aime-t-il… ?)

With a question word: Où est-ce que tu habites ? / Où habites-tu ? · Quand va-t-il à la banque ?

3. Trouvez la question

You get the answer — write the question. Look at the underlined part to choose the question word, and change the person (je → tu, nous → vous, mon → ton).

Answer tells you…Use
a personQui
a thing / actionQu'est-ce que / Que
a placeOù
a timeÀ quelle heure / Quand
a reason (parce que)Pourquoi
a way / meansComment
a number / priceCombien
a choice (which)Quel / Quelle / Quels / Quelles
yes / noEst-ce que…
Je me lève à sept heures.

À quelle heure est-ce que tu te lèves ? / À quelle heure te lèves-tu ?

Il va à la banque.

Où est-ce qu'il va ? / Où va-t-il ?

Je vais à l'école en bus.

Comment est-ce que tu vas à l'école ?

Elle retire de l'argent parce qu'elle va faire du shopping.

Pourquoi est-ce qu'elle retire de l'argent ?

4. La négation — mettez au négatif

Put ne before the verb and the second word after it (ne → n' before a vowel).

NegativeMeaningExample
ne … pasnotJe ne mange pas.
ne … jamaisneverIl ne se lève jamais tôt.
ne … plusno longer / not any moreNous n'habitons plus ici.
ne … riennothingJe ne vois rien.
ne … personnenobodyElle ne connaît personne.
Where does ne…pas go?
• Reflexive: around pronoun + verb → Je ne me couche pas.
• Futur proche: around aller → Je ne vais pas partir.
• Impératif: Ne parle pas ! Ne te lève pas !
• After a negative, un / une / des / du / de la → de (d'): J'ai un compte → Je n'ai pas de compte.
Mettez au négatif : Je regarde la télé.

Je ne regarde pas la télé.

Mettez au négatif : Il a une carte bancaire.

Il n'a pas de carte bancaire.

Mettez au négatif : Nous nous levons tôt.

Nous ne nous levons pas tôt.

Mettez au négatif : Elle va ouvrir un compte.

Elle ne va pas ouvrir de compte.

Use ne…jamais : Tu bois du café.

Tu ne bois jamais de café.

Useful phrases at the bank

📝 Practice sheet: 15 fresh questions on this topic

🗼 Section D : Culture & Civilisation

These are the 15 questions from your class sheet. In the exam, answer with a full sentence that repeats the words of the question, exactly like the model answers below.

How to answer: Quelle est la capitale de la France ? → Paris est la capitale de la France. (not just "Paris"). Nommez des… → list 3–4 names + sont des…

1. All questions and answers

#QuestionAnswer
1Quelle est la capitale de la France ?
What is the capital of France?		Paris est la capitale de la France.
Paris is the capital of France.
2Quel est l'hymne national de la France ?
What is the national anthem of France?		La Marseillaise est l'hymne national de la France. Elle a été composée en 1792 par Rouget de Lisle.
La Marseillaise is the national anthem of France. It was composed in 1792 by Rouget de Lisle.
3De quelle couleur est le drapeau français ?
What colour is the French flag?		Le drapeau français est bleu, blanc et rouge.
The French flag is blue, white and red.
4Quand est la fête nationale de la France ?
When is the national day of France?		Le 14 juillet est la fête nationale de la France.
The 14th of July is the national day of France.
5Quelle est la monnaie de la France ?
What is the currency of France?		L'euro est la monnaie de la France.
The euro is the currency of France.
6Nommez des fromages français.
Name some French cheeses.		Le camembert, le roquefort, le brie et le gruyère sont des fromages français.
Camembert, Roquefort, Brie and Gruyère are French cheeses.
7Nommez des vins français.
Name some French wines.		Le bordeaux, la bourgogne, le beaujolais, le champagne sont des vins français.
Bordeaux, Burgundy, Beaujolais and Champagne are French wines (named after regions).
8Nommez des pays francophones.
Name some French-speaking countries.		La Belgique, la Suisse, le Luxembourg et l'Algérie sont des pays francophones.
Belgium, Switzerland, Luxembourg and Algeria are French-speaking countries.
9Nommez les pays voisins de la France.
Name the neighbouring countries of France.		Les pays voisins de la France sont la Belgique, le Luxembourg, l'Italie, l'Espagne, la Suisse et l'Allemagne.
France's neighbours are Belgium, Luxembourg, Italy, Spain, Switzerland and Germany.
10Nommez des fleuves français.
Name some French rivers.		Le Rhône, le Rhin, la Seine, la Garonne sont des fleuves français.
The Rhône, the Rhine, the Seine and the Garonne are French rivers.
11Nommez des montagnes en France.
Name some mountains in France.		Les Pyrénées, les Alpes, le Jura et les Vosges sont des montagnes en France.
The Pyrenees, the Alps, the Jura and the Vosges are mountains in France.
12Nommez deux parfums français.
Name two French perfumes.		Chanel, Christian Dior, Yves Saint Laurent, Guerlain sont des parfums français.
Chanel, Christian Dior, Yves Saint Laurent and Guerlain are French perfumes.
13Pourquoi appelle-t-on la France « l'Hexagone » ?
Why is France called “the Hexagon”?		On appelle la France « l'Hexagone » parce qu'elle a plus ou moins la forme d'un hexagone.
France is called “the Hexagon” because it more or less has the shape of a hexagon (6 sides).
14Nommez des villes françaises.
Name some French cities.		Paris, Marseille, Lyon, Lille, Nice, Bordeaux et Toulouse sont des villes françaises.
Paris, Marseille, Lyon, Lille, Nice, Bordeaux and Toulouse are French cities.
15Quel fleuve traverse Paris ?
Which river flows through Paris?		La Seine traverse Paris.
The Seine flows through Paris.

ℹ️ Hymne is masculine, so it's l'hymne national. La Marseillaise is feminine, so elle a été composée.

2. The map of France

France has 6 sides (that's why it's l'Hexagone): 3 on the sea (la Manche, l'océan Atlantique, la mer Méditerranée) and 3 on land (neighbours and mountains).

3. Memory tricks

TopicTrick
🇫🇷 FlagBleu – Blanc – Rouge, left to right. The French football team is called les Bleus.
🎆 14 juilletBastille Day — the storming of the Bastille prison in 1789, start of the French Revolution.
🎵 La Marseillaise1792 (three years after 1789), by Rouget de Lisle. Soldiers from Marseille sang it → "Marseillaise".
🗺️ Neighbours (6)Go clockwise from the top: B – L – A – S – I – E → Belgique, Luxembourg, Allemagne, Suisse, Italie, Espagne.
🏔️ Mountains (4)P A J V → "Papa Aime Jouer au Volley": Pyrénées, Alpes, Jura, Vosges.
🌊 Rivers (4)"Rose et Remi Sautent Gaiement": Rhône, Rhin, Seine, Garonne. The Seine crosses Paris.
🧀 Cheeses (4)"Ce Rat Boit Gentiment": camembert, roquefort, brie, gruyère.
🌐 Francophone countriesBelgium, Switzerland and Luxembourg are neighbours that also speak French + Algeria in North Africa.
🏙️ Cities (7)Follow the map: Lille (north) → Paris → Lyon → Marseille & Nice (south coast) → Toulouse → Bordeaux (west).
💶 MoneyL'euro (€) since 2002 — before that, the franc.

5. Vrai ou faux ?

a) La Loire traverse Paris.

❌ Faux — la Seine traverse Paris.

b) La fête nationale de la France est le 14 juillet.

✅ Vrai.

c) L'Allemagne est un pays voisin de la France.

✅ Vrai.

d) La Marseillaise a été composée en 1789.

❌ Faux — en 1792, par Rouget de Lisle.

e) Le drapeau français est rouge, blanc et vert.

❌ Faux — il est bleu, blanc et rouge.

f) Le brie est un fromage français.

✅ Vrai.

⭐ Extra — beyond the Half Yearly syllabus. Useful for later and for higher marks in writing, but not required for this exam.

1. Passé composé — talking about the past

The passé composé is how you say what you did or what happened (I ate, she went, we watched). It is made of 2 parts:

helper verb (avoir or être) + past participle
J'ai + mangé = I ate  •  Elle est + allée = She went

Step 1 — pick the helper verb

Most verbs use avoir. Only a small group use être — mostly verbs about moving / going somewhere, plus being born and dying.

avoir (most verbs)être (special group)
j'ai
tu as
il / elle a
nous avons
vous avez
ils / elles ont		 je suis
tu es
il / elle est
nous sommes
vous êtes
ils / elles sont
The être verbs come in opposite pairs — learn them that way:
aller ↔ venir (go / come) • arriver ↔ partir (arrive / leave) • entrer ↔ sortir (go in / go out) • monter ↔ descendre (go up / go down) • naître ↔ mourir (be born / die) • rester ↔ tomber (stay / fall)
+ the "re-" versions: retourner, rentrer, revenir, devenir
+ all reflexive verbs (se lever → je me suis levé).

Step 2 — make the past participle

Verb ends in…Change it to…Example
-er-éparler → parlé (talked)
-ir-ifinir → fini (finished)
-re-uvendre → vendu (sold)

Some common verbs are irregular — learn them from the tables below.

Step 3 — only with être: add -e / -s to match the person

With avoir, the past participle never changes. With être, it changes like an adjective: add -e for a girl, -s for more than one.

Who?AddExample
one boynothingIl est allé
one girl-eElle est allée
boys / mixed group-sIls sont allés
only girls-esElles sont allées
Put it together: Hier, j'ai regardé un film, puis je suis sorti avec mes amis. (Yesterday I watched a film, then I went out with my friends.)
Negative: put ne…pas around the helper verb — Je n'ai pas mangé. Elle n'est pas venue.

Quick check: "We ate" in French?

Nous avons mangé. (manger uses avoir, so no agreement).

2. Futur simple and imparfait

Futur proche (going to): aller + infinitive: Je vais jouer au foot demain.

Futur simple (will): stem + -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont. Regular stem = the infinitive (-re verbs drop the e): parler → je parlerai, finir → je finirai, vendre → je vendrai. Irregular verbs have a special stem (see the table above): être → je serai, avoir → j'aurai, aller → j'irai, faire → je ferai, venir → je viendrai, voir → je verrai.

Imparfait (was doing / used to): take the nous form, remove -ons, add -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient. nous faisons → je faisais. Only être is irregular: j'étais.
